heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings (two uniform 256-bit words each); their chaining values CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: for every fixed variant a0, Pr[W7x in F7] = p7 = 287,309,824/2^32 exactly, and given it (W0..W6) is uniform and independent of W7 (Lemma 5.1); E16x is uniform for a good pair, so a lane passes the 8 tested bits with probability 2^-8 and the row-16 set with probability 160/2^32; the expected numbers of passing classes (0.53516) and good pairs (13,152) per first block; independence across first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected counts per first block that fix the work (V_MAX), the law of the second-block words that defines q3, and the independence of the first blocks (proof.md Sections 5 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact distribution of the number of passing classes over all 2^32 values of A_{-1} for the 8 classes (p8hits.c, Appendix A.2); 29,360,128 (2^22 + 2^23 + 2^24) real first blocks through the attack's own filters with the 8 classes (proof.md Section 13.1, e2ep8.c): passing classes, good pairs and stage-3a passes within 0.07% of their expectations, 14,199 row-16 passes against 14,385.0 expected (z = -1.55), every one checked exactly in Python (the first block gives the chaining value, the variant is selected, rows -4..16 hold in both members); the organizer experiment a0-online-r38.
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on 2^24 first blocks, not 2^82. The class tests of one first block are correlated (at most 2 of the 8 classes pass); only the expectations and the exact probability that some class passes enter the ledger.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 196,608 selected variants (the 8 classes of mask 7fe96c7c) of Pr[the pair is in the accepted event: rows 16..21 of both members follow every cell, '+' pair and two-bit condition of P8 closing at rows 16..21, row 19 on its signed differences only, and the state words A34..A37, E34..E37 of the two members are equal]; q3 >= q3_model = 2^-96.5755.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our preregistered measurement (proof.md Section 7.4 and Appendix A.9; preregistration hashed before the first seed): traillab, 32 fresh seeds x 2^28 window samples on real compressions with the real message expansion, row 16 exact (the 160-word set), W8 drawn from the 196,608 selected variants, W6 uniform, W7 uniform in F7, the accepted event counted (prefix rows 16..21 times zero output difference): mean 2^-96.3251, seed sd 0.577, declared one-sided 99% Student lower bound 2^-96.5755, halves -96.314 / -96.337, every diagnostic 0. Our replica (an independent implementation, Section 7.3): 960 calibration replicates, mean 2^-96.3095, every success rebuilt into a verified 38-step semi-free-start collision and accepted by the counted program; the organizer experiment a0-q3-r38 runs it with a pass rule frozen before its calibration (pooled mean of 20 >= 2^-97.0). 1a695f0b's estimator for its event (quoted): mean 2^-96.3683 over 20 runs. No transfer between classes or events is used.
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo lower bound measured with our own tool, which is not shipped (65,536-byte source limit); the replica and 1a695f0b's estimator are other implementations whose means agree with it within 0.05 bit. The replica estimates a lower bound (row-19 proposals from 1a695f0b's twelve conditions, W23 in F23, the characteristic's path from row 22). The bound treats the 32 seeds as independent replicates (the seed is the cluster); the mean of per-seed log2 values is conservative for log2 q3 (Jensen).

heuristics.statement: Let R_f be the number of selected variants of first block f that are good and pass row 16, and A_t the event that trial t = (f, a0) succeeds. Averaged over successes, the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times: sum_t Pr[A_t] E[R_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-7.5 E[X_f].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= E[X_f] - E[X_f (X_f - 1)]/2 >= (1 - 2^-8.5) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Under H1 the law of (CV1, a0) given a success is the law of the successes of the Step-3 sampler (proof.md Section 13.5). Our measurement on successes of the accepted event: 12,028 successes of 8 independent runs of the replica's sampler (all 8 classes, a0 uniform on the 196,608 variants), each rebuilt into a verified pair and accepted by step3b, every selected variant of every passing class of its chaining value tested: 32 other row-16 passes against 21.95 under independence, 2^-8.55 per success, one-sided 99% upper bounds 2^-7.97 (Poisson) and 2^-7.79 (Student over the 8 runs), below the premise; the stage-3a passes of the other variants are at 1.0008 of their expectation. 1a695f0b measured 2 other row-16 passes on 750 successes (quoted).
heuristics.limitations: The successes are sampled by the replica's sampler, a sub-event of the accepted event (row-19 relation sets, W23 in F23, zero differences from row 22), not real collisions; successes within a run share ancestors (the Student bound uses the 8 independent runs). The other row-16 passes exceed independence by a factor 1.46 (z = +2.15); the premise counts row-16 passes only, which is conservative. No organizer execution.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^78 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^78 is the largest allowance (0.28% of T); it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (78.09276).
heuristics.extrapolation: P8's search is published with its run log (1a695f0b Section 3.2, quoted; participant-run): 38 solver runs of at most 10,800 s (230,183 s in all), P8 found in 4,714 s with a 662-s coupling check; its author bounds the search, S, the class data and all development by one 10-core machine for less than 2^21 core-seconds, which at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second is 2^43.61 units, 34.4 bits under A_C. Our own measurements of the same kind of search (proof.md Appendix C, from fb176310): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units. A_C is fb176310's value, kept for the same accounting; 1a695f0b charges 2^48.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance, not our measurement: we did not rerun P8's search; its log and the 2^21 core-second bound are the author's. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 86.70961.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) and the 8 class descriptors with their product description are obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^74 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^74, 0.018% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: 1a695f0b obtained the pair in its 662-s coupling check and the class descriptors by 32 passes over a hash of c7 (quoted); our exhaustive pass over all 2^32 values of a0 (p8fam.c, 102 s, 69 MB peak) reproduces the 8 classes and their 24,576 members each, and selftest checks the product description. A_S is fb176310's value.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance: the pair search was run by 1a695f0b, not by us; its memory (2^28.094, measured by its author) sets the claimed peak (H6).

heuristics.statement: All development of this package (exhaustive passes, end-to-end runs, the q3 runs, the replica's development and calibration, the H3 measurement, the program scans; failed trials and reruns included) is at most DEV = 2^70 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^70, 0.0011% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: Recorded development below 10^5 CPU-seconds (proof.md Section 13.4); at 10^10 word operations per CPU-second that is below 2^50 operations = 2^38.3 compressions, so 2^70 is more than 2^31 times the recorded work. The peak memory of every development program whose results are used is measured, at most 2^27.48 bytes (proof.md Section 14 (c); two earlier, discarded versions of evidence programs held larger tables).
heuristics.limitations: Accounting of our own runs, not an organizer log; declared here because the review of fb176310 recorded it as an implicit heuristic (H-implicit-development-bound).

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, a straight-line word-RAM program that evaluates E16x = C16 + W0 + s0(W1) and its stage-3a test for 256 variants at once (bit L of every 256-bit word belongs to variant L) is charged its instruction list: every load, store and spill is counted, 64 registers, complements are free except in a mixed and/or (one more operation), no fused AND-NOT; one program per batch, with the batch's constant bits of a0 folded into it; no target compression is evaluated this way.
heuristics.scope: The plane-program term of the ledger (55,979.62 of the 62,939.17 data-dependent operations per first block).
heuristics.extrapolation: The 768 programs are generated and counted by experiments/a0lean38.py (build_e16, Prog.schedule, run_prog): 1,067 to 1,102 instructions per batch, no spill stores; every one of them is executed by the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 on all its 256 lanes and compared with the scalar definition (196,608 lanes per request in the local emulation, 0 mismatches), as are the batches of the passing classes of its trials 0..5 and 6 sampled batches in selftest.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited; the same reading was accepted for fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2. Program generation is charged 2^32 operations per program, not counted instruction by instruction. With a scalar evaluation (38 operations per variant) the claim would be 89.42650.

heuristics.statement: The peak memory is max(online, preprocessing) <= 2^28.1 bytes (claim memory_log2_bytes = 28.1): the online program needs 26,674,912 bytes (2^24.67: the code of the 768 batch programs at 32 bytes per instruction, the tables, planes and state); the largest preprocessing computation is the Step-1 solve of P8, measured by its author at 279,720 KB = 2^28.094 bytes; every other preprocessing computation and every development program is smaller.
heuristics.scope: The memory metric of the claim and the score 86.47433 + (28.1 - 20) = 94.57433.
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 14 lists every online component; the computations behind P8 measured by 1a695f0b (Step-1 solve 2^28.094, signed search at most 2^27.92, class descriptors 2^25.14; single-threaded, sequential, quoted); our solver instances (fb176310: 2^26.82 to 2^27.56); our development programs measured with /usr/bin/time -v (largest: the trail tool at 4 threads, 2^27.48); the organizer experiments run within the 128 MiB sandbox (35 MB and 27 MB peaks locally).
heuristics.limitations: The 2^28.094 figure is the author's sampled measurement (every 0.2 s), not ours; the machine model defines no code size (32 bytes per instruction is the generous choice).

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is a verified collision of the target (Lemma 6.1, proof.md Section 6.1).

Algorithm: the two-block attack of ePrint 2026/1120 with the characteristic P8 of dariolina's 1a695f0b (its cells, its semi-free-start pair and the Step-1 solution S; member x = M) and the A0-variant method of fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2: 8 classes of 24,576 variants (mask 7fe96c7c, 1a695f0b's selection); one W7 test decides a class, every variant of a passing class is a good pair; 768 straight-line batch programs (the batch's constant bits of a0 folded) evaluate E16x for 256 variants and test the 8 lowest bits shared by the 160 row-16 words; passing lanes resolved in scalar form; a row-16 pass is checked through row 21, row 19 on its signed differences only; rows 22..37 are computed untested and the output words of both members compared (proof.md Section 6.1).

Cost: fixed caps. N_FB = 4,449,581,490,679,991,464,212,814 first blocks (2^81.87994), each one target compression plus 35 counted operations, and V_MAX = 280,057,231,556,008,856,988,397,824,874 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded, tested at the start of every first block and after every class; at most V_MAX + 72,777,454, proof.md Lemma 8.1); allowances A_C = 2^78, A_S = 2^74 and the development charge DEV = 2^70 (H4a, H4b, H4c); counted precomputation 2^41.585 operations; final verification. Counted program: experiments/a0lean38.py (768 batch programs of 1,067 to 1,102 instructions, 2,829 operations for a row-16 pass). Exact total 2^86.4743228 (proof.md Section 11, Appendix B), claimed 86.47433.

Success probability at least 0.39 (the bound is exactly 0.39) under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-96.5755 for the accepted event of proof.md Section 6.1: the one-sided 99% lower bound of our preregistered measurement over the 196,608 selected variants; mean 2^-96.3251) and H3 (averaged over successes, the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times; measured 2^-8.55), by Bonferroni per first block, independence across first blocks and Chebyshev for the work cap; a cap halt happens only if the total work exceeds V_MAX, probability at most P_cap 4.84e-31, inside the bound (proof.md Section 10). No expected-work bound is used.

Memory: peak 2^28.1 bytes = max(online 26,674,912 bytes, preprocessing: the Step-1 solve of P8 measured by its author at 2^28.094 bytes; H6, proof.md Section 14). Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 86.47433 + 8.1 = 94.57433. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.
